# Curated multi-condition clip set

This directory holds the **curated multi-condition video fixture corpus** — the
decisive de-risk for the whole milestone (see `01-CONTEXT.md`). It exercises the hard
cases that clean single-dog footage hides: multi-dog scenes, a prominent handler,
tunnel/contact occlusion, jump/sprint motion blur, a distant dog, backlit/dusk light,
and the equidistant-midfield contention case — for **both disc dog and agility**.

The video binaries are **kept local and un-committed** (gitignored). Only this README
and the YAML manifest are tracked. See "Why footage is not committed" below.

## License

Real competition / community footage may be copyrighted or require the consent of the
people and dogs filmed. **You are responsible for the rights to every clip you drop in.**
Record provenance per clip in the table below (mirror it in the generated
`clip_manifest.yaml` `source` / `license` fields).

| Clip (relative to this dir) | Source        | License / Consent                              |
| --------------------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `disc_dog/<name>.mp4`       | user_footage  | Owner consent on file (describe / link here)   |
| `agility/<name>.mp4`        | user_footage  | Owner consent on file (describe / link here)   |
| `disc_dog/<name>.mp4`       | pexels        | Pexels License (CC0-like, commercial OK)       |
| `agility/<name>.mp4`        | pixabay       | Pixabay License (free commercial)              |

**Source values** (match the manifest schema): `user_footage`, `pexels`, `pixabay`,
`yt_dlp_cc`. **Allowed license refs:** `user_consent_README` (consent documented in
the row above), `cc0`, or a free-text reference into this table.

- Real user / community competition footage stays **local and un-committed** — never
  redistribute copyrighted footage through the repo.
- CC0 stock (Pexels / Pixabay) used only to **supplement missing conditions** (see the
  ingest procedure) is also kept out of git; the manifest records its provenance.

## Drop-location convention

Footage lives under this directory, organised by discipline. The cataloguer infers the
discipline from the sub-directory name, so the layout is the contract:

```
tests/fixtures/
  disc_dog/   <clip>.mp4   (+ optional <clip>.tags sidecar)
  agility/    <clip>.mp4   (+ optional <clip>.tags sidecar)
  README.md            (committed — this file)
  clip_manifest.yaml   (committed — generated by the cataloguer)
```

Recognised video extensions: `.mp4`, `.mov`, `.avi`, `.mkv`, `.m4v`, `.webm`. These are
gitignored under `tests/fixtures/**`; the README and `clip_manifest.yaml` are negated
back in so they stay tracked.

### Condition tags

Tag each clip with the conditions it exercises by writing a sidecar `<clip>.tags` file
next to it (comma- or newline-separated). The checklist (both disciplines) is:

`multi_dog`, `handler_prominent`, `tunnel_contact_occlusion`, `jump_sprint_blur`,
`distant`, `backlit_dusk`, `midfield_equidistant`.

Example — `disc_dog/toss_multidog_01.tags`:

```
multi_dog, handler_prominent, distant
```

## Ingest procedure

The footage path is **provided at execution time, never hardcoded**. You pass it to the
cataloguer as a command-line argument:

1. **Drop footage** into `disc_dog/` and `agility/` under this directory (see the
   layout above), and write a `<clip>.tags` sidecar for each clip.
2. **Run the cataloguer**, passing your footage directory as the argument:

   ```
   python tools/catalog_clips.py <footage_dir> --out tests/fixtures/clip_manifest.yaml
   ```

   It probes each clip's metadata via opencv (no `ffprobe` needed), infers the
   discipline from the sub-directory, reads the `.tags` sidecars, and writes
   `clip_manifest.yaml`.
3. **Review the coverage gap report** the tool prints — a `{condition × discipline}`
   matrix flagging every missing cell.
4. **Supplement missing cells** with CC0 clips from Pexels or Pixabay (see
   `.planning/research/STACK.md` → "Datasets & Test Fixtures"), drop them under the
   right discipline sub-dir, tag them, and re-run the cataloguer. Record each clip's
   license in the table above.

Later phases query the committed manifest to select clips by condition + discipline via
`segugio.fixtures.select_clips(...)` / `coverage_report(...)`.

## Why footage is not committed

- **Rights / consent** — competition footage may not be license-clear; committing it
  could redistribute material you don't have the right to share.
- **Repo size** — video binaries bloat the repo, and `git-lfs` is not installed.

The **external-dir + committed-manifest** pattern keeps the repo lean and license-safe:
binaries stay local; the manifest + this README carry provenance and the ingest recipe
so a fresh checkout knows exactly where to place footage and how to catalogue it.
